title: Plastic That Never Goes Away: The Ocean's Growing Emergency
title_zh: 永不消失的塑料：海洋日益严峻的危机
intro_zh: 本文约810词，聚焦塑料污染对海洋生态的严重危害，从塑料来源、微塑料污染到立法与个人行动，提供具体数据和案例，帮助读者理解环保紧迫性。

paragraphs.en: Every year, millions of tons of plastic waste end up in the ocean. We use plastic for almost everything – from bags and bottles to packaging and toys. Since the 1950s, plastic production has grown rapidly, reaching about 380 million tons per year today. Its convenience makes our lives easier, but we rarely think about what happens after we throw it away. This article explores how our daily convenience has created a serious environmental emergency beneath the waves.
paragraphs.zh: 每年，数百万吨塑料垃圾最终流入海洋。我们几乎把塑料用于一切——从袋子、瓶子到包装和玩具。自20世纪50年代以来，塑料生产迅速增长，如今每年约达3.8亿吨。它的便利让生活更轻松，但我们很少去想扔掉之后会发生什么。本文探讨我们日常的便利如何在波涛之下制造了一场严重的环境危机。

paragraphs.en: How does plastic reach the ocean? Much of it flows from rivers, especially in countries where waste collection systems are poor. If no proper garbage collection exists, plastic simply gets dumped into waterways during storms. Wind blows litter from beaches and streets into rivers and the sea. Lost fishing nets and gear, known as 'ghost gear,' also make up a large portion of marine debris. These items, once useful, become part of a tragic marine trash problem.
paragraphs.zh: 塑料是如何到达海洋的？其中大部分来自河流，尤其是在垃圾收集系统不完善的国家。如果没有适当的垃圾收集系统，塑料就会在暴风雨中被直接冲入水道。风把海滩和街道上的垃圾吹进江河和大海。丢失的渔网和渔具，被称为“幽灵渔具”，也构成了海洋垃圾的很大一部分。这些物品曾经有用，现在却成为海洋垃圾问题的一部分。

paragraphs.en: Unlike organic materials, plastic is remarkably persistent. Most common plastics do not biodegrade; they remain in the environment for hundreds of years. Sunlight and waves break them into smaller pieces, but they never truly disappear. As a result, plastic accumulates in the ocean, forming giant circular currents called gyres. One famous example is the Great Pacific Garbage Patch, a huge area of floating debris located between California and Hawaii. It is estimated to be twice the size of Texas, containing more than 79,000 tons of plastic. Whirlpools and currents trap the trash, making it difficult to clean up.
paragraphs.zh: 与有机材料不同，塑料具有极强的持久性。大多数常见塑料不会生物降解；它们能在环境中存留数百年。阳光和海浪将它们分解成更小的碎片，但它们永远不会真正消失。结果，塑料在海洋中堆积，形成巨大的环流，称为“涡流”。一个著名的例子是“太平洋垃圾带”——一片位于加利福尼亚和夏威夷之间的大面积漂浮碎片区。据估计，它的面积是德克萨斯州的两倍，含有超过7.9万吨塑料。漩涡和洋流困住垃圾，使其难以清理。

paragraphs.en: Marine animals suffer greatly from this pollution. Sea turtles often mistake plastic bags for jellyfish and ingest them, blocking their stomachs and causing starvation. Seabirds feed plastic pieces to their chicks, which can lead to dehydration and death. Research on albatrosses shows that many chicks have plastic in their stomachs from their parents' feeding. Many animals become entangled in abandoned fishing lines and nets, preventing them from swimming or hunting effectively. Seals, dolphins, and even whales are victims of entanglement, which can cause drowning or slow starvation.
paragraphs.zh: 海洋动物深受这种污染之苦。海龟常把塑料袋误认为水母并吞食，堵塞胃部导致饥饿。海鸟把塑料碎片喂给雏鸟，可能导致脱水和死亡。对信天翁的研究显示，许多雏鸟胃里有父母喂食的塑料。许多动物被废弃的渔线和渔网缠住，无法正常游泳或捕食。海豹、海豚甚至鲸鱼都是纠缠的受害者，可能导致溺水或慢慢饿死。

paragraphs.en: An even more hidden danger is microplastic. These tiny particles, smaller than five millimeters, come from broken-down plastic, synthetic clothing fibers, and exfoliating personal care products. Microplastics float nearly everywhere in the ocean and are readily ingested by plankton, the very base of the marine food chain. Through this process, plastic enters the bodies of fish, shellfish, and eventually humans who consume seafood. Recent studies have found microplastics in table salt, drinking water, and even human organs. While the health effects are not yet fully understood, they may carry harmful chemicals that disturb our bodies.
paragraphs.zh: 一个更隐蔽的危险是微塑料。这些小于五毫米的微小颗粒来自分解的塑料、合成衣物纤维和去角质个人护理产品。微塑料几乎漂浮在海洋各处，很容易被浮游生物摄入，而浮游生物正是海洋食物链的基础。通过这一过程，塑料进入鱼类、贝类甚至食用海鲜的人类的体内。最近的研究在食盐、饮用水甚至人体器官中发现了微塑料。虽然对健康的影响尚未完全明确，但它们可能携带干扰人体机能的有害化学物质。

paragraphs.en: The scale of the problem is staggering. Scientists estimate that about 8 million metric tons of plastic enter the ocean every year. That is equivalent to dumping a garbage truck full of plastic into the sea every minute. If current trends continue, studies suggest that by 2050, there could be more plastic than fish in the ocean, by weight. Moreover, only nine percent of all plastic ever produced has been recycled. The rest ends up in landfills, incinerators, or the natural environment, with a huge share reaching the ocean. This is not just an environmental issue, but also a threat to human health and economies that depend on oceans.
paragraphs.zh: 问题的规模令人震惊。科学家估计，每年约有800万吨塑料进入海洋。这相当于每分钟就有一辆满载塑料的垃圾车倒入大海。如果当前趋势继续下去，研究显示到2050年，按重量计算，海洋中的塑料可能比鱼类还多。此外，所有塑料中只有9%被回收利用。其余的最终进入垃圾填埋场、焚烧炉或自然环境，其中很大一部分流入海洋。这不仅仅是环境问题，也是对依赖海洋的人类健康和经济的威胁。

paragraphs.en: Fortunately, there is growing awareness and action. Many countries have introduced legislation to ban single-use plastics like straws and plastic bags. For example, the European Union voted to ban various disposable plastic items by 2021. Businesses are developing eco-friendly alternatives, such as recyclable packaging and biodegradable materials made from corn or seaweed. Researchers are also creating enzymes that can efficiently break down PET plastic, offering a promising solution for recycling. International initiatives, like the United Nations' Clean Seas campaign, aim to reduce marine litter and encourage governments to pledge action.
paragraphs.zh: 幸运的是，人们的意识和行动正在增强。许多国家已出台立法，禁止使用吸管和塑料袋等一次性塑料。例如，欧盟投票决定到2021年禁止多种一次性塑料制品。企业正在开发环保替代品，如可回收包装和由玉米或海藻制成的可生物降解材料。研究人员还在创造能高效分解PET塑料的酶，为回收提供了有希望的解决方案。联合国‘清洁海洋’运动等国际倡议旨在减少海洋垃圾，并鼓励各国政府承诺采取行动。

paragraphs.en: As individuals, we can also make a difference. Carrying reusable bags, refusing plastic straws, and properly disposing of trash are simple habits. Supporting local policies that reduce plastic production and improve recycling also helps. Taking part in beach cleanups is another direct way to remove trash from the environment. Additionally, choosing products with less plastic packaging can send a clear message to manufacturers. While the damage already done to the ocean is immense, we have the power to stop it from getting worse. Every small step away from plastic brings us closer to cleaner seas.
paragraphs.zh: 作为个人，我们也能有所作为。随身携带可重复使用的袋子、拒绝塑料吸管、正确处理垃圾，这些都是简单的习惯。支持减少塑料生产和改进回收的当地政策也有帮助。参加海滩清理是另一种直接清除环境垃圾的方式。此外，选择塑料包装较少的产品可以向制造商传递明确信息。尽管海洋已经遭受巨大破坏，但我们有能力阻止情况恶化。远离塑料的每一小步，都让我们更接近更清洁的海洋。

paragraphs.en: The ocean covers more than 70 percent of our planet and is vital for life on Earth. It regulates our climate, provides food, and generates over half of the oxygen we breathe. By thinking carefully about the plastic we use, we can help protect marine ecosystems and our own future. The tide of pollution is high, but human action can turn it. Governments, companies, and citizens all have a role to play. It is not too late to act, but time is running out.
paragraphs.zh: 海洋覆盖我们星球70%以上的面积，对地球生命至关重要。它调节我们的气候，提供食物，并产生我们呼吸的超过一半的氧气。仔细思考我们使用的塑料，就能帮助保护海洋生态系统和我们自己的未来。污染浪潮高涨，但人类的行动可以扭转局面。政府、企业和公民都可以发挥作用。现在行动还不算太晚，但时间所剩无几。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: A. Plastic is convenient but harmful to human health.
B. Plastic pollution has become a serious threat to oceans and requires action.
C. The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is the largest landfill in the world.
D. We should completely stop using plastic in our daily lives.
questions.explain: 文章主要讲述塑料污染对海洋的严重危害以及个人和社会可采取的应对行动，故选B。A只是部分内容，C过于具体，D过于绝对。

questions.q: According to the passage, how does plastic reach the ocean?
options: A. Only through illegal dumping from ships.
B. It is carried by rivers from areas with poor waste management.
C. It is naturally produced in the ocean.
D. It comes from underwater volcanic eruptions.
questions.explain: 第二段明确指出“Much of it flows from rivers, especially in countries where waste collection systems are poor.”，故选B。其他选项文中未提及。

questions.q: What can be inferred about microplastics?
options: A. They are harmless to marine animals.
B. They can enter the human food chain through seafood.
C. They only exist in the Pacific Ocean.
D. They are larger than plastic bottles.
questions.explain: 第五段说微塑料被浮游生物摄入，进而通过食物链进入鱼类、贝类和人类体内，故选B。A与文意相反，C过于绝对，D说大于塑料瓶错误。

questions.q: The word “ingest” in Paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to:
questions.explain: 根据上下文“Sea turtles often mistake plastic bags for jellyfish and ingest them”可知海龟把塑料袋当水母吞食，所以ingest意为“摄取，吞食”，与eat最接近。
